name: GGUF Q4_K_M (4-bit K-quant, medium)
quality_delta: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.56 vs 7.32 F16 (+0.24, the smallest perplexity cost of any 4-bit option measured); GSM8K 69.41 vs 77.63; IFEval 72.35 vs 78.93; unweighted mean 69.15 vs 69.47 (-0.46% AvgLoss); size 4685 MiB (-69.41%).
notes: The most widely used llama.cpp quant and the default in most tutorials. Important structural point most blog posts get wrong: Q4_K_M is *not* pure 4-bit weights - at 4.8944 bpw it is wider than Q5_0's advertised class and wider than the classic Q4_0, because the k-quant super-block spends real bits on quantized sub-block scales/mins. That is where its quality advantage comes from, not from clever rounding. Weight-only: activations stay in FP16/BF16 at runtime, so there is no '4-bit activations with hardware support' claim to make here. ggml has bespoke dequantize+gemm kernels per type, but no accelerator has a GGUF/k-quant path in silicon; everything is dequantized on the fly. vLLM explicitly labels its GGUF support experimental and under-optimized and positions it as a memory-footprint tool (quant-vllm-gguf-doc). In that study Q4_K_S dominates Q4_K_M on both axes (more reduction, lower AvgLoss), which is the opposite of the conventional 'Q4_K_M is better than Q4_K_S' folk rule - recorded as contested rather than resolved.
